title_ar: الشيخ الددو يدعو لتحرير العالم الإسلامي من هيمنة الغرب | قمة كوالالمبور
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Calls for Freeing the Muslim World from Western Domination | The Kuala Lumpur Summit
body_ar:
شارك فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو عضو مجلس أمناء الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين ونائب رئيس منتدى كوالالمبور للفكر والحضارة، في الندوة الأولى من ندوات مؤتمر حول تحديات التنمية والحلول المقترحة .

وتأتي الندوة ضمن جلسات “القمة الإسلامية المصغرة”، والتي تحتضنها هذه الأيام العاصمة الماليزية كوالالمبور .

والتقى الددو على هامش الجلسة الافتتاحية لأعمال القمة مع بعض الشخصيات المشاركة.

وقال الددو في كلمته “إن منتدى كوالالمبور أنشئ بهدف التفكير لإيجاد حلول غير مستوردة، تخرج الأمة الإسلامية مما هي فيه”، مضيفا أن التفكير بالأمة يكون بقدر القناعة بها ودخولها في كيان الإنسان معللا: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد ربى أصحابه على التفكير بالأمة (ومن أمثلة ذلك قصة الأذان وقصة الخندق).

واستفهم الددو كيف تكون خير أمة أخرجت للناس بهذا الوضع؟ وعلق قائلا أن الأمة الإسلامية هي التي أرست قواعد العدالة وحقوق الإنسان ورسخت قيم العدل والإحسان والحرية والسلام والتعايش ونصرة المظلوم، وفتقت أفنان الحضارة وفنون الثقافة.

وأكد الددو “إن المضطهدين والمظلومين من هذه الأمة في سجونهم ومنافيهم لا يجدون من يواسيهم ويتحدث باسمهم غير هؤلاء الرجال الثلاثة: سمو الأمير الشيخ تميم بن حمد وفخامة الرئيس رجب طيب أردوغان ودولة رئيس الوزراء الدكتور مهاتير بن محمد”.

وأوضح الددو أن أبرز تحديات التنمية تتمثل في “عدم استقلال قرار دول العالم الإسلامي، والتخلص من الدكتاتوريات المفسدة التي لا تحسن غير تعذيب الشعوب ونهب الخيرات ويدعمها أشباهها وأسيادها على تدمير البلاد والعباد”.

وبحسب الددو “فإن الحروب التي يوقد نارها الأعداء فتهلك الحرث والنسل، والمجموعات الإرهابية التي لا تخدم إلا الأعداء، واحتكار القوى الكبرى للتكنولوجيا والصناعة والعلوم، هي تحديات تواجه تنمية العالم الإسلامي”.

وأضاف تحديات أخرى مثل “جهل كثير من المسلمين بأمور دينهم وفهمهم له فهما خاطئا، والارتباط بالعملة الأجنبية التي تتحكم في أسعار صرف عملاتنا والتلاعب باقتصادنا، الفساد المالي والإداري”.

وأقترح الددو في كلمته جملة مقترحات للتنمية منها “السعي لإيجاد مرجعية إسلامية جامعة والعمل على تغيير أنظمة المنظمات الدولية، وضرورة إسقاط الأنظمة الدكتاتورية بالوسائل السلمية، واللجوء للحوار والتحكيم في كل المسائل الخلافية”.

كما طالب الددو في مقترحاته “بمحاربة الإرهاب بالفكر لتحصين الشباب وبالحوار العلمي مع أصحاب هذا الفكر عن طريق العلماء المتمكنين، وإصلاح المناهج التعليمية والتركيز على تدريس التكنولوجيا والعلوم بمختلف أقسامها، إقامة مؤسسات علمية تتعهد بتعليم الدين وترسيخ مفاهيمه الصحيحة تكون قادرة على المنافسة”.

ومن بين المقترحات أيضا “السعي لإيجاد بديل عن الدولار يتمثل في الذهب سواء كان كمادة أو كعملة إسلامية موحدة، وكذا محاربة الفساد الإداري والمالي بوضع القوانين الصارمة وتطبيقها ومحاربة المحسوبية وتشغيل الكفاءات والأشخاص المناسبين في الأمكنة المناسب”.

يذكر أن جلسات وأعمال القمة مستمرة حتى الـ21 ديسمبر الجاري.

المصدر: الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, member of the board of trustees of the International Union of Muslim Scholars and vice-chairman of the Kuala Lumpur Forum for Thought and Civilisation, took part in the first of the conference panels on the challenges of development and the solutions proposed.

The panel comes within the sessions of the "Islamic mini-summit", which the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur is hosting these days.

On the margins of the opening session of the summit, al-Dedew met some of the participating figures.

In his address al-Dedew said: "The Kuala Lumpur Forum was established with the aim of thinking in order to find solutions that are not imported, solutions that will bring the Muslim Ummah out of the state it is in." He added that one thinks about the Ummah in proportion to one's conviction about it and to its entering into one's very being, explaining that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had trained his Companions to think about the Ummah (examples being the story of the call to prayer and the story of the Trench).

Al-Dedew asked how it could be the best community brought forth for mankind while in this condition, and commented that it was the Muslim Ummah that laid the foundations of justice and human rights, that established firmly the values of justice, excellence, freedom, peace, coexistence and support for the wronged, and that opened out the branches of civilisation and the arts of culture.

Al-Dedew affirmed: "The persecuted and the wronged of this Ummah, in their prisons and their places of exile, find no one to console them and to speak in their name other than these three men: His Highness the Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad, His Excellency President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and His Excellency the Prime Minister Dr Mahathir bin Mohamad."

Al-Dedew explained that the most prominent challenges to development lie in "the lack of independence in the decision-making of the states of the Muslim world, and ridding it of the corrupting dictatorships which are good at nothing but torturing peoples and plundering resources, and which are supported by their like and by their masters in destroying countries and people."

According to al-Dedew, "the wars whose fire the enemies kindle, so that they destroy crops and progeny; the terrorist groups which serve none but the enemies; and the monopolisation by the great powers of technology, industry and the sciences — these are challenges confronting the development of the Muslim world."

He added further challenges such as "the ignorance of many Muslims about the affairs of their religion and their mistaken understanding of it; dependence on the foreign currency which controls the exchange rates of our currencies and the manipulation of our economy; and financial and administrative corruption."

In his address al-Dedew proposed a number of proposals for development, among them "striving to bring into being a comprehensive Islamic authority of reference and working to change the systems of the international organisations; the necessity of bringing down the dictatorial regimes by peaceful means; and recourse to dialogue and arbitration in all contested questions."

Al-Dedew also called in his proposals for "combating terrorism by means of ideas, so as to fortify the young, and by scholarly dialogue with the holders of this ideology through capable scholars; reforming educational curricula and concentrating on the teaching of technology and the sciences in their various branches; and establishing scholarly institutions which undertake to teach the religion and to establish its sound concepts firmly, and which are able to compete."

Among the proposals also was "striving to find an alternative to the dollar, consisting in gold, whether as a commodity or as a unified Islamic currency; and likewise combating administrative and financial corruption by laying down strict laws and applying them, combating favouritism, and employing those who are competent and the right persons in the right places."

It may be noted that the sessions and proceedings of the summit continue until the 21st of this December.

Source: the International Union of Muslim Scholars

flags.arabic: وضرورة إسقاط الأنظمة الدكتاتورية بالوسائل السلمية
flags.context: among the proposals for development in the Sheikh's address
options: hold the record from publication pending review
publish the report as translated, with the qualifier 'by peaceful means' kept prominent
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. The report has the Sheikh calling for dictatorial regimes to be brought down, and names three sitting heads of state and government favourably in the same address while characterising unnamed others as corrupting dictatorships that torture their peoples. In several jurisdictions in which this corpus will be read, that is material a state could treat as hostile, and in the West it raises no criminal question but does raise a reputational one and, as to the unnamed regimes, no defamation risk while they are unnamed. The qualifier بالوسائل السلمية, 'by peaceful means', is in the Arabic and is decisive; it has been kept in the English exactly where the Arabic puts it and must not be dropped at display time. Nothing has been softened or strengthened.

flags.arabic: وأقترح الددو في كلمته جملة مقترحات
flags.context: the opening of the tenth paragraph
options: read as واقترح, 'and al-Dedew proposed', as rendered here
mark the word as corrupt and leave it unrendered
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. أقترح is first person ('I propose') where the third person اقترح is required by the following subject الددو. A hamzah slip. Preserved in body_ar, recorded here, not silently fixed.

translator_notes: فتهلك الحرث والنسل echoes Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:205; rendered literally as 'destroy crops and progeny' because the allusion is the point. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
خير أمة أخرجت للناس echoes Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:110 and is rendered 'the best community brought forth for mankind'.
مرجعية إسلامية جامعة is a comprehensive Islamic authority of reference — an institution to which questions are referred — not a 'unified Islamic reference'.
الأمكنة المناسب appears in the source with the adjective unagreed (for الأمكنة المناسبة). Preserved in body_ar.

A news report of an address. It states no ruling and engages no category of the five rulings; ضرورة here is ordinary Arabic 'necessity' in the sense of 'what is needed', not the technical threshold the glossary defines, and has been rendered accordingly.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this slice carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1038/1039/1040 at 08:13/08:14/08:14 on 8 August 2019; 1077/1078/1079 at 09:50/09:52/09:53 on 22 July 2020), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
